page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E6.Ax.Flex.4-32 is a general-purpose virtual machine shape built on the x86_64 architecture. It provides 8 vCPUs running on 4 dedicated physical cores of an AMD EPYC 9J45 processor with a clock speed of 2.7 GHz and two threads per core. The server includes 32.0 GB of memory, delivering an even allocation of 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU.

Hardware provisioning does not include local disk storage, which necessitates the attachment of remote block volumes for persistent data and operating systems. The instance also lacks GPU accelerators, being designed purely for central processor workloads. Network connectivity includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

The 1:4 compute-to-memory balance makes VM.Standard.E6.Ax.Flex.4-32 appropriate for enterprise application deployment, middle-tier services, web serving, build execution, and general processing tasks that do not depend on high-speed local NVMe storage or graphics hardware.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E6.Ax.Flex.4-32 is a general-purpose compute instance based on the x86_64 architecture. Powered by an AMD EPYC 9J45 processor operating at 2.7 GHz, the virtual server provides 8 vCPUs derived from 4 dedicated physical cores with 2 threads per core. System memory is sized at 32.0 GB, establishing a standard 1:4 processor-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. The configuration contains no local storage devices, requiring attached block volumes for system and data persistence, and features no GPU acceleration. A single complimentary public IPv4 address is included. Designed for reliable execution across balanced resource profiles, the VM.Standard.E6.Ax.Flex.4-32 fits typical general-purpose workloads, including application servers, microservices architectures, web hosting, and background batch tasks.
